pageProps.content: ## Ordered ```menu { "title": "Zuburasoba", "rating": 3 } --- A soupless, thick stir-fried soba style with a subtle hint of mala flavor, but not overly spicy—just the right level of heat. ``` ```menu { "title": "Original Tonkotsu", "rating": 3.5 } --- The broth was very rich and the noodles were on the thinner side; while it was tasty, it was a bit underwhelming as it wasn't particularly better than the ramen spots in Seoul. ``` ## Review This was our very first meal after driving hard since dawn for our trip to Geoje. When looking up good restaurants in Geoje, locals said there weren't many great food spots around, but we usually enjoy eating just about anything, so we didn't worry too much. While pondering where to eat for our first meal, we settled on ramen, which felt like a relatively light option. Looking at restaurant reviews, it had high ratings and usually drew quite a line, so we figured a Friday lunch would be less crowded than the weekend and decided to check it out. ```adcard ``` The restaurant was located in a villa building, and parking was available right at the building. I was worried parking might be difficult since it's a residential villa building, but to my surprise, there was enough space to accommodate around eight cars. Moreover, there were strangely almost no cars belonging to the residents, so we were able to park easily without any issues. Arriving early before opening by moving quickly also seemed to help. ` Even though we arrived 20 minutes before opening, the doors were already open, and we could place our order right away via the kiosk. It was emphasized here that even when waiting in line, you must place your order first before waiting, and before opening was no exception. We ordered the Zuburasoba and the Original Tonkotsu. ```adcard ``` After placing the order and completing the payment at the kiosk, an order slip comes out; you write down your contact phone number on it and drop it into the black bin next to the kiosk. Since it was still before opening hours, we spent some time taking a light stroll around the neighborhood after ordering. Right on opening time, they called the phone number we had written down, and we were finally able to enter the restaurant. The interior was relatively small with only a few tables, which gave it an authentic, cozy feel reminiscent of a local eatery in Japan. Inside the shop, an old Japanese documentary-style variety show was playing continuously. It followed an ordinary office worker struggling while working at a ramen shop to open a franchise; I watched closely wondering if it had any connection to this restaurant, but couldn't find any particular link. ```adcard ``` After sitting down and waiting for a short while, the dishes we ordered came out promptly. The Zuburasoba was a soupless style, reminiscent of fried soba where the sauce coats the noodles thickly. The mala aroma came through very subtly without being too spicy, making it comfortable and enjoyable to eat. The Tonkotsu Ramen had a very rich broth, and the noodles were on the thinner side. To be honest, compared to the ramen I frequently enjoy in Seoul, it was certainly delicious, but I didn't feel it was exceptionally superior, which left me slightly disappointed. Still, tasting the rich broth brewed with care allowed me to appreciate the owner's sincerity and hard work. It seems like a place worth stopping by at least once when visiting Geoje. However, since the weekend wait times are said to be huge, you might want to plan carefully, and personally, I don't think it's worth waiting in line for 1 to 2 hours. ## Pictures
